source_evidence: By purchasing municipal bonds, you are in effect lending money to the bond issuer in exchange for a promise of regular interest payments, usually semi-annually, and the return of the original investment, or “principal.” A municipal bond’s maturity date (the date when the issuer of the bond repays the principal) may be years in the future.
answer: Municipal bond interest and principal are paid at different times. The issuer usually makes regular interest payments semi-annually. The maturity date is when the issuer repays the original investment, called the principal; that date may be years away. The source describes short-term bonds as maturing in one to three years and long-term bonds as maturing in more than a decade.
